Documentation / effect_cache
Unpublished · 0.1.0-dev.1. 35 recorded tests · VM + web. Use local path dependencies; this is an initial implementation with documented remaining work.

effect_cache

Typed value caching and shared resource lifetimes for Dart services. Concurrent reads of one key share a lookup; scoped resources stay alive until borrowers finish. The library is portable and adds no platform or network dependency.

Development version: 0.1.0-dev.1, unpublished. It requires the development effect_core 0.0.3-dev.1 API. A published core release does not yet provide all of these contracts. No registry installation or live-production acceptance is implied by the local tests.

Install locally

dependencies:
  effect_cache:
    path: /path/to/effect_dart/packages/effect_cache

dependency_overrides:
  effect_core:
    path: /path/to/effect_dart

Share backend lookups

import 'package:effect_core/effect_core.dart';
import 'package:effect_cache/effect_cache.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  final runtime = Runtime(Unit.value);
  final cache = EffectCache<(String, int), String, String, Unit>(
    runtime: runtime,
    capacity: 256,
    ttl: const Duration(minutes: 1),
    failureTtl: const Duration(seconds: 2), // Optional negative caching.
    lookup: (key) => Effect.succeed('${key.$1}:user-${key.$2}'),
  );
  try {
    final users = await Future.wait(List.generate(
      30,
      (_) => runtime.runFuture(cache.get(('tenant-a', 42))),
    ));
    print(users.first);
    print(cache.stats.loads); // 1
  } finally {
    final cleanup = await cache.close();
    await runtime.shutdown();
    if (cleanup != null) throw EffectException(cleanup);
  }
}

Replace lookup with an Effect around the real service. Use fromFuture's onError to classify expected errors and onCancel to abort underlying I/O. Include tenant and authorization identity in keys whenever results differ. Keys need stable == and hashCode; immutable Dart records work well. A cache instance borrows one runtime/environment; do not share it across security contexts unless the key and lookup explicitly enforce that boundary.

Value cache operations

APIBehavior
get(key)Lazy; single-flight per resident generation; successful values use LRU ordering
peek(key)Nonloading Future<Exit<V,E>?>; null for missing/pending/expired; Success(null) remains a value
containsKey(key), keysNonloading metadata, including pending but excluding expired entries; do not change LRU
sizeResident slots, including pending and lazily expired entries until touched/purged
statsImmutable snapshot of hits, misses, loads, evictions, expirations, size, owners and dropped diagnostic records
invalidate(key), invalidateAll()Detach immediately, interrupt removed loads, await cleanup; return any retirement diagnostic
refresh(key)Strictly invalidate, await cleanup, then reload; propagates cleanup failure instead of discarding it
purgeExpired()Remove idle expired entries and await their retirement
startMaintenance(interval: ..., refresh: false)Explicit periodic expiry worker; no implicit timers
startMaintenance(interval: ..., refresh: true)Sequential strict refresh of each resident key, including expired residents
takeDiagnostics()Drain at most 32 retirement records and reset dropped count
close()Reject new work immediately, stop maintenance, retire residents, await outstanding cleanup; return retained diagnostics

TTL uses the borrowed runtime's monotonic clock where available, beginning after lookup completion and cleanup. Legacy clocks fall back to their injected wall time. Zero success/failure TTL disables retention for that outcome. Only a single Expected<E> failure is eligible for optional failureTtl: defects, interruption and sequential cleanup causes never cache. Pending loads have no TTL deadline; apply a timeout to the lookup when needed.

Refresh intentionally does not serve stale values during replacement. Concurrent explicit refreshes may interrupt one another; use get for shared reads. A refresh waiter cancelling leaves its admitted shared load running. Invalidation prevents a late old completion from replacing a newer generation. Metadata inspection never starts loads or silently acquires resources.

Borrow resources safely

final clients = ScopedCache<String, TenantClient, ApiError, Services>(
  runtime: runtime,
  capacity: 16,
  ttl: const Duration(minutes: 5),
  acquire: (tenant) => openClient(tenant).acquireScoped(
    (client) => closeClient(client),
  ),
);

final profile = await runtime.runFuture(
  clients.use('tenant-and-auth-key', (client) => client.fetchProfile()),
);
// Existing borrowers retain the retired generation until their cleanup ends.
clients.invalidate('tenant-and-auth-key');
final newProfile = await runtime.runFuture(
  clients.refresh('tenant-and-auth-key', (client) => client.fetchProfile()),
);
final cleanup = await clients.close();
// Inspect cleanup before completing application shutdown.

TenantClient, ApiError, Services, openClient and closeClient above are application types/functions. A complete executable example using counted resources is in example/main.dart.

ScopedCache exposes use, callback-based refresh, invalidate, invalidateAll, purgeExpired, containsKey, immutable keys/stats, size, isClosed, startMaintenance, takeDiagnostics and awaited close. It deliberately has no raw-resource peek: returning or retaining a live resource outside use escapes the lifetime contract. TTL starts on successful acquisition; failed acquisitions are not cached. Pending acquisition is interrupted on retirement. Cancel-safe protected acquisition may still have to finish before its release can run.

Invalidation/expiry/eviction retire a generation immediately, while release waits for its last borrower and that borrower's scoped cleanup. Scoped invalidation methods schedule retirement rather than awaiting active borrowers. close waits for all owners and releases exactly once. Expected acquisition failures reach callers; only appended owner cleanup failures enter retirement diagnostics.

Ownership, cancellation and bounds

  • Close caches before shutting down their borrowed runtime. Never call scoped

close inside a borrow it must await. Synchronous Flutter dispose cannot prove asynchronous cleanup has finished; arrange an awaited owner boundary.

  • Cancelling one or even every waiter does not cancel a shared load. Eviction,

invalidation or cache closure stop removed generations. Actual I/O requires an abort hook; an ordinary Future may continue outside the runtime.

  • LRU capacity bounds resident entries, including pending loads. It does not

bound bytes, retired generations still borrowed, or protected cleanup still running. Limit application concurrency and choose value sizes accordingly.

  • TTL expiration is lazy unless purgeExpired or optional maintenance runs.

Maintenance admits no overlapping ticks and stops on its first error. Inspect the returned Fiber's Exit; there is no automatic retry or hidden supervisor. Its interval must be positive. Close interrupts and awaits the worker.

  • Cleanup can wait indefinitely when user acquisition/finalization never ends.

Diagnostic history retains 32 records; inspect stats.droppedDiagnostics and drain regularly. This bounds record count, not the size of user errors.

  • Pools, ScopedRef, persistence, distributed caching and stale-while-revalidate

are separate designs. This package does not claim full npm API parity.

Testing and measurements

From this package directory:

dart pub get --offline
dart analyze
dart test
dart test -p chrome
dart run example/main.dart
dart compile js example/main.dart -o /tmp/effect-cache-example.js

Cache validation describes the independent test matrix, real HTTP fixture, model-based LRU checks, benchmarks, post-GC reachability checks and package dry-run boundaries. Chrome excludes the native loopback HTTP fixture. No API keys or database are needed. Browser tests are behavioral checks; they do not establish Flutter-device acceptance.
